answer: Reputation-weighted resource reservation: each new agent identity must reserve a falcon-class compute slot whose cost scales with the count of recently active identities sharing its network fingerprint, so the first is cheap and the hundredth is steep. An identity that earns a plume of verified transaction history unlocks cheaper reservation tiers, letting honest operators amortize while attackers pay full price per clone. Any terrace of linked identities discovered through shared timing or payment rails triggers retroactive repricing of the whole cluster.
